correctness.rationale: Reconstructed both directions for nonempty finite structures with exactly one total unary function f and equality and ONE reusable variable symbol. At depth d every term equality pattern of x,f(x),...,f^d(x) is one bounded (preperiod,period) type or the no-visible-repeat type; a formula reduces by quantifier induction to Boolean tests of which such types occur. If a realized type set includes a transient point or a no-visible-repeat orbit, attaching leaves to an appropriate existing cycle creates only already realized types and every larger cardinality, hence a tail. Otherwise each element is on a permitted visible cycle and exact sizes are s(L)+<L>. Explicit one-variable universal/existential formulas realize every such cycle semigroup, every tail T_N, and the empty spectrum; finite disjunction realizes all finite unions. Checked d=0, N=1 and L nonempty; no finite experiment used to prove an infinite theorem.
residual_risks: Bibliographic priority versus recent FO1 model-counting work is qualified, but no mathematical gap found in the two-way argument.

evidence: Durand–Fagin–Loescher show arbitrary FO with one unary function has the entire eventually periodic spectrum family.

broader_coverage.reasoning: A more expressive logic having all eventually periodic spectra does not imply every ultimately periodic set is realizable in the strictly one-variable fragment or identify the exact subfamily. The Grandjean terminology has a different formal meaning.

value.rationale: An exact all-sentence expressive-power classification for a canonical restricted logical vocabulary. The cycle-length semigroup structure is not an arbitrary numeric slice; it identifies precisely the realizable finite model cardinalities, excludes e.g. odd-only spectrum by multiplication closure, and exposes what loss of a second variable does. A useful positive/negative model-theoretic characterization, not a routine textbook consequence of eventual periodicity.
residual_risks: May be a natural consequence of existing forward-profile methods; mathematical motivation remains even if priority reduces.

limitations: Nonempty finite models only; one total unary function and equality, no other symbols or constants.
Single reusable variable symbol, not one universal quantifier or counting quantifiers.
Priority comparison includes limited-full-text older source and recent profile-counting corollary risk.
